answer: When new registrations surge like a tide, scarce admission seats sit on a rising knoll: the bond to claim one seat scales with recent join volume. Claiming a seat also forces a live verification kernel that re-solves a peer-chosen prior task under a fresh seed. A sybil farm facing a high tide must lock capital for every knoll seat and pass distinct kernel checks in parallel, so clones cost stake times the inflated bond, not a flat signup fee.
